Research designMixed methodsAI communication
Explore the study +

Comparing Sustainability Communication Strategies in AI Shopping Conversations

A 98-participant study completed for the MA in Cognition and Communication at the University of Copenhagen. The thesis received 12/12.

What it shows

Experience with formulating a research question, comparing communication approaches, analysing quantitative and qualitative evidence, and presenting the findings with appropriate limits.

A careful conclusion

The study did not find a significant overall difference between conditions. It should not be read as evidence that one approach improves sustainable choices.

MAKING COLLABORATION WORK
02 / REALLAB / COPENHAGEN BUSINESS SCHOOL

Good collaboration
needs more than a match.

Research into the practical work behind collaboration between students, academics and companies, with project lead Peren Özturan.

InterviewsResearch synthesisStakeholder needs
Explore the project +

My contribution

As a student researcher, I supported interview recruitment, research materials, transcription and follow-up, analysis and the presentation of insights.

From conversations to coordination

The study covered 14 participants across 15 interviews. Preliminary analysis highlighted matching, scoping, data access, communication and the coordination work that often goes unseen.

What the work points toward

A coordination layer that helps people clarify expectations and preserve knowledge across projects. This is a research direction, rather than a claim of a finished platform.

LOOKING BEYOND THE ANSWER
03 / COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH / 2026

What does a helpful
AI answer actually do?

Research with Frans van der Sluis on how AI assistants support responsible product search and decision-making.

AI evaluationInteraction researchShort paper submitted
Explore the research +

From Retrieval to Responsible Choice

An audit of AI assistants for responsible product search, examining communication and interaction support across shopping scenarios.

Research focus

The work considers how assistants retrieve information, explain evidence and support responsible alternatives. The short paper has been submitted to CHIIR 2027; it is not presented here as an accepted publication.

Scope

System conditions differ, so the audit is not a causal ranking of assistants. It also does not establish the factual accuracy of every product claim.

Based in Copenhagen. Open to opportunities in communication, marketing and project coordination.
